Chapter 7. Estimation and Correction

Source: vignettes/articles/07-Estimation-and-Correction.Rmd
07-Estimation-and-Correction.Rmd

decant() runs three steps in order. Each is also available as its own function, which is useful when you want to inspect or replace one of them.

Step Function Output
1. Soup profile ambient_global() Fraction of ambient RNA per gene
2. Contamination estimate_rho_cluster() rho per cell, with per-cluster diagnostics
3. Correction correct_counts() Corrected counts

7.1 Step by step 

library(Decant)
sim <- simulate_experiment(seed = 1)

soup <- ambient_global(sim$empty)
round(sum(soup), 6)
#> [1] 1

rho <- estimate_rho_cluster(sim$observed, soup, clusters = sim$labels)
round(median(rho), 3)
#> [1] 0.199

corrected <- correct_counts(sim$observed, soup, rho,
                            method = "bayes_cell", clusters = sim$labels)
  • ambient_global() sums the empty droplets gene by gene and divides by the total, giving a soup profile that adds up to 1.
  • estimate_rho_cluster() finds the genes each cluster does not express and measures how much soup explains their counts (Chapter 2.5). It returns one value per cell.
  • correct_counts() removes rho × cell total × soup from each cell, using the rule given in method.

7.2 How rho is estimated

For each cluster, Decant repeats two steps until they agree:

  1. Using the current rho, test every gene: is its count in the cluster clearly above what the soup alone would give? Genes that are not are called absent.
  2. Re-estimate rho from the absent genes only: the ratio of their observed counts to their expected soup counts.

Five safeguards make the estimate reliable on real data:

  • Gene-to-gene spread is allowed for. In real data, absent genes do not sit exactly on the line rho × soup: they scatter around it by about 25-30%, because soup and capture differ slightly from gene to gene. Step 1 therefore uses a negative binomial test whose extra spread is measured from the lowest absent genes, which expressed genes can never reach. A plain Poisson test would reject the absent genes that fall above the line and keep those below, and the estimate would settle at about half the true value. With no extra spread the test is the Poisson test.
  • Enough expected counts. A gene enters the absent set only if enough ambient counts are expected for it (min_expected = 5). Without this, thousands of rarely detected genes look absent simply for lack of counts, and rho is overestimated.
  • Per-cell shrinkage. Each cell’s rho is pulled towards its cluster’s rho, more strongly for cells with few counts. Small cells therefore do not get extreme values.
  • Weak clusters borrow. A cluster without enough absent genes (low_power) borrows rho from the other clusters instead of guessing.
  • Implausible values are not trusted. A cluster whose estimate exceeds 0.5 (implausible) would be mostly soup, which happens when the soup looks like the cluster’s own expression. It borrows rho too. If most cells are in such clusters, rho cannot be estimated from the data at all, and decant() warns (Chapter 11.4).

7.3 The five correction rules

Rule How it removes contamination When to use
bayes_absent (default) First decides, gene by gene and cluster by cluster, whether the cluster expresses the gene at all; a gene it does not express loses all its counts. Otherwise as bayes_cell. Where the two groups of genes overlap, it does not decide and behaves as bayes_cell General use; removes the most on species mixtures, about the same as bayes_cell in real tissue so far
bayes_cell Assigns each count to cell or soup by how well each explains it, cell by cell. Counts far too high to be ambient keep all but their ambient expectation Keeping the most native signal
bayes The same, but one ratio for the whole cluster Reproducing earlier results
redistribute Removes exactly rho × total counts per cell, in soup proportion (SoupX’s approach) Comparing with SoupX
subtract Subtracts the expectation gene by gene and stops at zero Simplest reference; removes too little 
for (m in c("subtract", "redistribute", "bayes", "bayes_cell", "bayes_absent")) {
  r <- decant(sim$observed, sim$empty, clusters = sim$labels, correction = m)
  e <- score_correction(sim$observed, r$corrected, sim$truth)$l1_error
  cat(sprintf("%-13s %.3f\n", m, e))
}
#> subtract      0.067
#> redistribute  0.063
#> bayes         0.047
#> bayes_cell    0.049
#> bayes_absent  0.048
  • The loop runs Decant once per rule and prints the error against the truth (lower is better; no correction scores 0.245).
  • On this one simulation the three Bayesian rules are close. Across all simulated settings in gate_correction(), bayes_absent has the lowest average error, by a small margin over bayes_cell.
  • The difference shows on real mixtures of human and mouse cells, where the truth is known. On two 10x mixtures never used to design it, bayes_absent removed 0.891 of the ambient signal (bayes_cell 0.531, DecontX 0.655), and kept 0.9918 of the cells’ own signal (bayes_cell 0.9945). On the hardest mixture it kept 2.5 points less than bayes_cell. That is why it is the default, and why bayes_cell stays available: use correction = "bayes_cell" when keeping every native count matters more than removing the soup.
  • On real blood data (PBMC 4k) the clusters share most of their genes, the two groups overlap, and bayes_absent gives the same result as bayes_cell. Both keep the counts of likely doublets, which bayes removes.

7.4 The guarantee

Every rule satisfies 0 ≤ corrected ≤ observed for every gene in every cell. Decant checks this after each run and stops with an error if it were ever violated. Some other tools return corrected counts that are larger than the observed ones; Decant cannot.

7.5 Tuning parameters

The defaults were chosen on test data and rarely need changing.

Function Argument Default Effect
estimate_rho_cluster() alpha 0.01 Stringency for calling a gene expressed; smaller calls fewer genes expressed
estimate_rho_cluster() min_expected 5 Minimum expected ambient count for an absent gene
estimate_rho_cluster() floor_rho 0.005 Smallest contamination considered possible; also the lowest starting value
estimate_rho_cluster() max_rho 0.5 Largest contamination treated as identifiable
estimate_rho_cluster() overdispersed TRUE Allow for gene-to-gene spread of absent genes; FALSE gives the earlier Poisson test
correct_counts() cap_q 0.001 For bayes_cell and bayes_absent: how unusual a count must be before it is treated as not ambient
